item.title: Khloe Kardashian Recounts Saving Naked Lamar Odom From 20 Hookers Holding Him Hostage
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Khloe Kardashian says a chaotic hotel encounter during her marriage to Lamar Odom still shapes what she will not accept in dating.
item.content:encoded:
Khloe Kardashian says a chaotic hotel encounter during her marriage to Lamar Odom still drives her dating boundaries. She and Kris Jenner told the story on the November 5 episode of The Kardashians.

The memory came up during a truth-or-dare game with Kim Kardashian and her The Fifth Wheel co-stars. Jenner said the family got word that Odom was at a hotel during the height of his drug use.

She claimed they thought he was being held there against his will.

“We’re going to extract him from the situation because he’s being held hostage by these hookers,” Jenner recalled.

Kardashian said her security team entered the room first.

“And all I saw [was] they were literally having a circle jerk. There were 20 people in the room,” she said. She also said everyone was naked.

She said she rushed into the room and fought people. Jenner stayed in a bathroom and put drugs in trash bags. “I just lunge and start swinging, beating people up, and my mom is hiding in the bathroom,” Kardashian said on the show.

Kardashian framed the memory as a warning, not a reunion. She said the night still shapes the traits she will avoid in a man. She has also said she wants honesty and trust from any future partner.

The account adds detail to a marriage marked by public claims of infidelity and Odom’s substance use disorder. It is Kardashian and Jenner’s version of what happened that night.

Kardashian and Odom married in 2009. She filed for divorce in 2013. She withdrew the filing after Odom’s near-fatal 2015 overdose so she could help with his care. She filed again in 2016, and the divorce was final that December.

The two met on camera in 2025 after years apart. Their ties later broke down again. Kardashian said in April that their bridge was burned after she disputed parts of Odom’s Netflix film.

The Kardashians Season 8 is streaming on Hulu. New episodes arrive on Thursdays. People said Odom’s representative did not at once respond to a request for comment on this account.

item.title: RBX Appeals Spotify Bot-Streaming Lawsuit Dismissal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: RBX has appealed the dismissal of his Spotify bot-streaming lawsuit after a federal judge ended the case with prejudice.
item.content:encoded:
RBX has taken his bot-streaming fight with Spotify to a federal appeals court, extending a case that a Los Angeles judge dismissed last month.

The Long Beach rapper filed an appeal after U.S. District Judge Josephine L. Staton ended his amended class-action lawsuit with prejudice. The federal docket lists a November 6 notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.

RBX, whose legal name is Eric Collins, sued Spotify in 2025.

He alleged that the streaming company allowed artificial plays to distort the royalty pool and reduce payments to independent artists. His complaint cited suspicious activity involving Drake’s catalog as one example. Spotify was the sole defendant.

The dispute moved through two versions of the complaint. Judge Staton dismissed the first version in June and gave RBX time to amend it.

He returned in July with broader allegations about selective enforcement of Spotify’s anti-fraud rules and the effect that bot activity could have on artists who rely on the same royalty pool.

The revised complaint still failed to clear the legal bar. In the October order, Judge Staton found that RBX had not pleaded enough facts to support his unfair-competition and negligence claims. She entered judgment for Spotify after dismissing the case with prejudice.

AllHipHop covered that ruling, which closed the case at the trial-court level. The new filing moves the fight to the Ninth Circuit, where RBX can challenge the legal reasoning behind the dismissal.

The appeal keeps a larger music-industry issue in view. Streaming services have tightened enforcement against artificial plays, while independent artists have questioned how platforms detect fraud and protect royalty pools.

RBX built his case around the argument that enforcement was uneven and harmed artists outside the biggest commercial catalogs.

The appellate court will review the record made before Judge Stanton.

RBX’s lawyers can argue that the complaint met the legal standard and that the case should return to the district court for more proceedings. Spotify will have a chance to defend the judgment.

The notice of appeal begins the next stage of the case. The Ninth Circuit will set the briefing schedule and decide whether to affirm the dismissal.

item.title: Flyysoulja Revises Overdose Account, Citing Drug-Induced Psychosis
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Flyysoulja says his October 29 hospitalization involved drug-induced psychosis, correcting his earlier account of an overdose.
item.content:encoded:
Flyysoulja says his October 29 hospitalization was caused by drug-induced psychosis, not an overdose, correcting the account he gave after leaving a Miami trauma unit.

The Island Boys member, whose legal name is Alex Venegas, told TMZ that doctors reached the psychosis diagnosis. He had previously said a combination of cocaine, benzodiazepines and Percocet caused an overdose during a celebration for a new condominium and car.

Venegas spent four days in the hospital and was released on November 2. Venegas provided the new explanation. It changes the cause he gave for the emergency, not the fact that he received treatment.

The correction also fits a longer pattern of substance-related crises that Venegas has discussed publicly. In January, he said he was entering detox after another psychotic episode and wanted to take treatment more seriously.

“I’m going to detox right now to get the help I need. I can’t wait. I’ve been here before,” he said at the time.

That January step followed a November 2025 incident at his home. Venegas said he had taken several substances before damaging the property while broadcasting without realizing it.

“In the psychosis, I was trying to find something for my hair for hours, and destroyed the home while unknowingly being on Live,” he said after that episode.

He also drew a line between addiction and a lasting mental-health diagnosis, saying then that he had a substance problem. His latest account again links the episode to drug use while changing the medical label he originally attached to the October hospitalization.

The correction arrived days after a separate legal problem. Local 10 reported that Venegas was arrested November 2 on a petty-theft charge tied to an alleged March incident at a Hallandale Beach Walgreens.

Police accused him of leaving with $75.45 in merchandise. He posted bond, and the court has not yet decided the case.

AllHipHop’s November 2 report reflected Venegas’ first account. His new statement now replaces “overdose” with drug-induced psychosis as his explanation for why he spent four days receiving care.

item.title: BigXthaPlug Wants Rap To Be Fun Again As He Questions Drill’s Influence
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: BigXthaPlug says drill changed Hip-Hop's mood and argues rap needs more fun, range and room for artists to take risks.
item.content:encoded:
BigXthaPlug has a blunt diagnosis for the state of rap: the music has lost some of its fun, and the pressure to look tough has narrowed what artists think they can make.

The Dallas rapper laid out that argument during a Club Shay Shay conversation with Shannon Sharpe. He answered quickly when Sharpe asked whether rap was dying, then pointed to his own fast rise as evidence that the system is moving strangely.

“I been rapping five years. Ain’t no way I should be at the top,” BigXthaPlug said.

His point was not that he did not earn his success. He questioned how viral records can push newcomers into the same commercial conversation as veterans who spent years building careers. In his view, money and momentum now move faster than experience.

BigXthaPlug also argued that drill music changed the mood around Hip-Hop. He did not dismiss the artists or the sound. Instead, he said its influence helped create an environment where too many rappers feel they must be aggressive, even when a different direction might fit them better.

“It need to be fun again,” he said.

He pointed to Snoop Dogg’s pop collaborations as an example of a period when major rappers could stretch without treating every crossover as a threat to their credibility. The comparison was less about nostalgia than freedom. BigXthaPlug wants artists to try records that sound unexpected and still be accepted as rappers.

That position carries extra weight because BigXthaPlug has tested Hip-Hop’s borders himself. His country-inspired project I Hope You’re Happy debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200, while “All The Way” with Bailey Zimmerman reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart.

He has since returned to rap with Better Over Time, an 18-track album featuring GloRilla, Lil Yachty, Leon Thomas, Ava Max and others. AllHipHop attended his Dallas preview, where the album was paired with a short film and a surprise parking-lot performance.

His official site now presents Better Over Time as the main event, but the music around it moves through rap, R&B and pop. That variety makes his criticism more than an outside complaint. He is testing the openness he says the genre needs.

BigXthaPlug’s answer is not a demand for one sound to replace another. He is asking for room to experiment again, whether that means country, pop, storytelling or straight Texas rap. His own career shows why he believes moving outside one image can expand an audience without abandoning Hip-Hop.

item.title: Jalen Brunson Makes His ‘SVU’ Debut As Detective Jay Madison
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jalen Brunson made his SVU debut as Detective Jay Madison, giving Olivia Benson the break that moved a wedding assault case forward.
item.content:encoded:
Jalen Brunson finally got his Law & Order: Special Victims Unit moment, and the New York Knicks captain did more than walk through the frame. He played Detective Jay Madison, an off-duty cop whose memory helped Captain Olivia Benson break open the episode’s central case.

The cameo aired November 5 in Season 28’s fifth episode, “Forsaken.” NBC had announced Brunson’s guest spot in September but kept his role under wraps. The completed episode revealed a name that appeared to salute Madison Square Garden and gave him a short scene opposite Mariska Hargitay.

According to Entertainment Weekly’s episode account, Benson approached Madison about a sealed record tied to Rick Davis, the stepfather of a 16-year-old who was assaulted at a wedding. Madison had arrested Rick on charges that included drunken driving and resisting arrest.

Benson congratulated the detective on his promotion. Brunson answered with a line that sounded like it could have come from a postgame interview: “Focused on my goals, gave 110 percent, things worked out.”

The exchange quickly returned to police work. Madison recalled details from the arrest, including Rick’s behavior and a confrontation involving his teenage son. That information helped the squad narrow its focus, and the son was arrested for the assault by the end of the episode.

Brunson had been asking for this assignment since the Knicks won the 2026 NBA championship. When reporters asked what he wanted to do next, his answer was simple: “Try to get on ‘SVU.'”

The wish was not as random as it sounded. Brunson has spoken publicly about being a longtime fan of the series and Hargitay. She is also a committed Knicks supporter. The two appeared together during the Emmy Awards opening in September, days before NBC confirmed the November guest role.

The appearance continued a busy stretch outside basketball for Brunson. He hosted the September 26 season premiere of Saturday Night Live after leading New York to its first championship since 1973, becoming the fifth NBA player to host the show. The league also chronicled the SVU announcement as part of his expanding entertainment profile.

Brunson did not turn the scene into a comedy sketch or a basketball commercial. He played the job straight, delivered the clue and left Benson’s squad to close the case.

item.title: Cam’ron Explains Why He Chose Unpaid First Take Appearances
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cam'ron says he worked ESPN's First Take for free, using the exposure to build credibility and bring viewers to his own shows.
item.content:encoded:
Cam’ron says his appearances on ESPN’s First Take were never about collecting a quick check. He went on the network for free because the bigger prize was visibility, credibility and a chance to lead viewers back to the sports shows he controls.

The Harlem rapper laid out the strategy during REVOLT’s November 4 episode of Talk With Flee. Guests Symba and Aleyse Shannon were discussing the grind behind their acting careers when the conversation turned to the sacrifices that come before a bigger opportunity.

“I was going for free. I didn’t want no money right now. I wanted to show my value,” Cam’ron said.

He described taping his own show late at night, driving to Los Angeles, sleeping in his car and then reporting to ESPN early enough for the network’s morning broadcast. “It’s about the grind,” he said.

Cam’ron’s point was not that ESPN owed him nothing. It was that a familiar cable platform could validate his presence as a sports commentator while putting him in front of people who had not yet watched his independent work. He said the exposure could move some of that audience toward his own programming, where he has more control over the voice, format and business.

The size of that stage was real. ESPN said First Take averaged 564,000 viewers in May, up 18 percent from the same month in 2025. Cam’ron joined Stephen A. Smith and the show’s panel during that playoff run, including a May 12 debate over LeBron James and the Los Angeles Lakers.

That appearance demanded a different kind of discipline. Cam’ron said he remained himself but understood that he could not curse or treat Smith’s platform like his own set. He did not want his performance to damage somebody else’s opportunity or professional standing.

The tradeoff also explains why Cam’ron keeps returning to ownership. A network hit can open a door, but the long-term value sits in the audience that follows him back through it. His unpaid ESPN work was an investment in that transfer, not an admission that his time had no price.

item.title: Fetty Wap Reportedly Got Married In New Jersey
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Fetty Wap reportedly married Alexis Hill at a private New Jersey wedding where the groom performed “679.”
item.content:encoded:
Fetty Wap apparently had a strict guest list for his wedding, but somebody’s phone apparently made the cut.

The New Jersey rapper married Alexis Hill on Thursday, Nov. 5, according to an exclusive report from The Shade Room. The couple reportedly celebrated at the Legacy Castle in New Jersey with approximately 90 to 100 guests. Just months after their July engagement, they have made things official.

Now, about those phones. Sources told the outlet that guests’ devices were secured during the ceremony. I understand the appeal. Sometimes you want people watching you exchange vows, not selling the footage to TMZ.

But a little footage still reached the outside world. The Shade Room reported reviewing a video of Fetty performing “679” for his bride while she danced in a white strapless wedding gown and his large diamond chain. Alexis then moved in for a hug.

Must be nice. Performing your own hit at your wedding is a flex. Most grooms have to submit a request to the DJ or hire talent. And Alexis wearing the chain? That sounds like the jewelry equivalent of making herself at home.

In July, Alexis shared images and video featuring a large pink floral heart, tall candles and a rose petal aisle. She received pink roses along the way before reaching Fetty, who got down on one knee. She also showed her large square diamond engagement ring.

Clearly, somebody took the decorating budget seriously.

What catches my attention is the relatively small gathering. A recognizable Hip-Hop name, a castle venue and fewer than 100 or so guests sounds like a deliberate effort to keep the celebration close.

We don’t need to manufacture a scandal for every occasion. Sometimes the story is a rapper singing to his wife while she wears his chain.

Congratulations to Fetty and Alexis. Here’s hoping the marriage gets more privacy than the average celebrity relationship.

item.title: Elon Musk Puts Kibosh On Tesla Cybertruck
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.category: signs the world is coming to an end
item.description: Elon Musk’s Cybertruck is losing its factory space to robotaxis, begging the question: Is Tesla’s futuristic flex an epic fail?
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk has put an expiration date on the Cybertruck’s current production run, and I have questions for anybody who bought one expecting to drive the future.

Apparently, the future needs that parking space back.

Musk announced that Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around the middle of 2027 to accommodate more Cybercabs. Yes, the angular pickup that looks like it arrived with classified documents is being asked to make room for a robotaxi.

“Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production,” Musk wrote on X.

Before anybody starts engraving a stainless steel headstone, there is a detail worth keeping straight. Reuters reported that Musk did not specify whether production might move to another facility or stop altogether.

The Texas wind-down is announced. A permanent farewell requires a little more clarity. It does not look great, we have to admit.

This is quite the development for a vehicle designed to command attention at every traffic light. I was never impressed. You cannot quietly pull up in something that resembles a refrigerator preparing for combat. LOL!

The business backdrop tells the real story.

Reuters reported that the Cybertruck struggled to sustain buyer interest after its 2023 launch and faced recalls, quality issues and repeated pricing changes. We saw it all online. Some were easy to rip apart with bare hands. Others were pointless off road. Those are substantial problems for any vehicle, especially one that’s supposed to be a 4wd fancy whip.

How do owners feel watching Tesla prepare the factory for its next big idea? They gotta feel foolish. Are they going to be able to sell that sucker?

For now, owners can keep driving and hoping they keep some parts for when it breaks down or needs a spare tire.

They were never hard.

item.title: Doja Cat Examines Love And Jealousy Behind Vie With Jennifer Hudson
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Doja Cat discussed jealousy, love and personal growth behind Vie during her Jennifer Hudson interview as her North American tour continued.
item.content:encoded:
Doja Cat put the difficult side of romance at the center of her conversation with Jennifer Hudson, explaining how jealousy and relationship struggles fed into Vie.

During her November 6 appearance on “The Jennifer Hudson Show,” the rapper and singer described an album built around love without leaving out its harder emotions. She acknowledged her own capacity for jealousy while recognizing that it can hurt a relationship.

“with this album I wanted to touch on the more visceral parts of relationships, the hardships of it,” Doja Cat said.

The conversation also covered personal growth and her mental health, subjects she has addressed publicly while supporting the record. Her discussion with Hudson arrived as she continued the North American leg of Tour Ma Vie with Latto.

Vie, her fifth studio album, arrived September 26, 2025. Its lead single, “Jealous Type,” put that relationship theme directly in the title. Jack Antonoff and Y2K produced the track, and Boni Mata directed its Los Angeles-shot video.

The album followed Scarlet and moved toward an ’80s-inspired pop sound while keeping the singing and rapping that have shaped her work. Its French title translates to “life.” Love and identity run through the project, with “Jealous Type” setting up the romantic tension before the full record arrived.

Her mental health message provided further context for her recent discussion of growth. In August, Doja discussed past problems with cocaine and alcohol and the damage that online validation could do when she was already struggling.

She described the cocaine issue as years behind her. Her message focused on recognizing harmful coping habits and seeking help, rather than presenting those past experiences as her current condition.

Latto has also been part of this stretch of Doja’s career. The two released the video for their collaboration “Okayyy” in July, ahead of their fall arena dates together. The song appeared on Latto’s Big Mama album.

Their North American tour began October 1 in Detroit and is set to finish December 1 at Madison Square Garden. The run followed Doja’s overseas dates and brought her album campaign back to U.S. and Canadian arenas.

item.title: Casey Anthony Assists YNW Melly Defense Prep Ahead Of January Retrial
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: YNW Melly's legal team brought Casey Anthony into retrial preparations as a research assistant for a private investigator.
item.content:encoded:
Casey Anthony is assisting with preparation for YNW Melly‘s January 2027 double-murder retrial in Florida.

TMZ reports Anthony is working as a research assistant for private investigator Pat McKenna, whom the rapper’s law firm hired.

Her work involves researching parts of the case, although the team has not described the specific evidence or issues assigned to her.

Anthony and McKenna did not respond to the outlet’s requests for comment. YNW Melly’s legal team also did not explain how long Anthony has been involved in the preparation.

The rapper, whose legal name is Jamell Demons, faces two counts of first-degree murder in the October 26, 2018 deaths of Anthony Williams, known as YNW Sakchaser, and Christopher Thomas Jr., known as YNW Juvy.

Prosecutors allege Williams and Thomas were shot inside a vehicle and that the scene was made to look like a drive-by shooting. Demons has pleaded not guilty.

His first trial ended in a mistrial in July 2023 after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict. The retrial is set to begin January 6, 2027. Prosecutors are again seeking the death penalty if he is convicted.

Antonio Henry, known as YNW Bortlen, was charged alongside Demons. Henry pleaded guilty in September 2025 to accessory after the fact and witness tampering charges. He received a 10-year prison sentence followed by probation.

The defense added attorney Drew Findling this year. Findling joined the case after helping secure Lil Durk’s acquittal in a federal murder-for-hire trial.

AllHipHop previously reported that Findling criticized the length and conditions of Demons’ pretrial detention.

Anthony’s role connects McKenna to another high-profile criminal case. McKenna worked as a defense investigator during Anthony’s 2011 trial in Florida.

A jury acquitted her of murder, aggravated child abuse and aggravated manslaughter in the death of her daughter, Caylee.

She was convicted of four misdemeanor counts of providing false information to law enforcement, and two of those convictions were later overturned on appeal.

Demons has remained in custody since February 2019. His defense now has two months to finish its preparation before jury selection is scheduled to begin in January.
